title: A New Non-Affine Family in the Karlsson-Szollosi Intersection
abstract: We show that $K_6^{(2)} \cap X_6^{(2)} = D_6^{(1)} \cup C_6^{(1)}$ up to standard Hadamard equivalence, where $C_6^{(1)}$ is a new non-affine one-parameter family of complex Hadamard matrices. This demonstrates that the intersection of the two-parameter Hadamard families of Karlsson and Szöllősi is strictly larger than the known affine Diţă curve $D_6^{(1)}$. Our new parametrisation of the Szöllősi family $X_6^{(2)}$ in Karlsson coordinates and our constructive classification of the Karlsson-Szöllősi intersection shed light on the intersection of block-reducible forms and hypocycloid constraints. This may support the search for mutually unbiased bases in six dimensions.
summary: This paper rigorously classifies the intersection of two complex Hadamard matrix families in dimension six. By employing advanced algebraic geometry techniques, the authors prove that all solutions belong to the union of two specific one-parameter families: an affine curve and a newly discovered non-affine family. This result significantly advances the mathematical understanding of quantum state structures relevant to MUBs.
main_problem: The paper aims to classify the intersection of two specific two-parameter families of complex Hadamard matrices in dimension six: the Karlsson family $K(2)_6$ and the Szöllősi family $X(2)_6$. This classification is crucial for understanding the structure of these matrices.
main_result: The intersection $K(2)_6 \cap X(2)_6$ is shown to be exhaustively characterized as the union of two distinct one-parameter families: an affine Diţă curve $D(1)_6$ and a newly discovered non-affine family $C(1)_6$.
method: The authors employ advanced algebraic techniques, including Gröbner basis calculations on ideals generated by constraints derived from analyzing 'frames' associated with the matrices. They use parameter transformations and standard-equivalence certificates to prove the equivalence of different solution sets.
model_or_system: The study focuses on complex Hadamard matrices of order six, which are mathematical objects with direct applications in quantum information theory, particularly in the context of finding Mutually Unbiased Bases (MUBs) in six dimensions.
key_observables: The primary observables are the matrices themselves, characterized by parameters $(b, c, e, f)$ for the physical representatives $X$, and the classification of the supporting 'frames' (e.g., generic, Diţă, mixed).
important_parameters: The dimension $N=6$ is central. Key parameters include the defining parameters for the families, such as $(u, v)$ for $C(u, v)$ and the various phase/block parameters used in the parametrizations.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the physical solutions are fully captured by analyzing the 225 possible 'frames' and that the established standard-equivalence relations are sufficient to classify all solutions.
figures_summary: The figures illustrate the structure of the Karlsson sector subfamilies and provide detailed tables summarizing the classification of the 225 possible supporting frames, grouping them into types that map to $D(1)_6$ or $C(1)_6$.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the problem (Chunk 1), then deriving the explicit parametrization of the new family $C(1)_6$ and proving its inclusion in the intersection (Chunk 2). The core of the work involves an exhaustive classification of the supporting 'frames' using algebraic geometry (Gröbner bases) to show that all physical solutions fall into $D(1)_6 \cup C(1)_6$ (Chunks 3 & 4).
why_interesting: While the core is mathematical, the direct application to MUBs in quantum information theory makes it highly relevant. The rigorous classification of matrix families using algebraic geometry provides powerful, generalizable tools for analyzing quantum state structures.
